text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Islamists walk out of parliament after failing to extract announcement from government that it will halt normalisation of relations with Israel.
- Department for Combating Corruption confiscates telecommunication equipment illegally linked up to Israeli companies. .
- King Hussein and Crown Prince Hassan meet Israeli Labour leader Ehud Barak.
- Customs head says cuts in tariffs will be matched by increases in sales tax only in the case of cars.
- Why do we force King Hussein to repeat his call for administrative reform more than once?
- Senate calls for emergency Arab League meeting over Israel's settlement in East Jerusalem.
- Clearing company in Aqaba port complains over delays to its shipment to Iraq caused by Lloyds inspectors.
- Minister of Supply says it would take three years to abolish his ministry.
- Qatari Crown Prince arrives in Jordan on Wednesday.
- Prime minister says Israel endangers peace process and violates all agreements.
- Plight of four-year-old girl exposed conditions at orphanage in Jordan. Rejection of orphan by three hospitals and tip-off to royal court triggered king's action.
